pairs.difference: A: the yellow hull turns orange-brown underneath, with teal portholes and a deep green field. That is two clear hue roles, and shadow chroma holds at 0.90. B: the feeder is pure yellow and red-orange painted wood, and the lens merges all of it into one orange mass. The trunk shadows fall to dull brown (shadow kept 0.61, below the real range) and the park behind is washed out.
pairs.fix: Paint the feeder in natural weathered wood with a muted tan roof, not pure yellow and orange. Make the shadows under the roof a rich deep red-brown with a little violet, not dull brown.

pairs.difference: A: the horse, fence, dirt and mane are all one orange-brown family, and shadows on the belly and legs drop to dull dark brown (shadow kept 0.43, well below real). Only the sky breaks the warm mass. B: the red guitar sits against blue-violet stage trusses, with cream as a neutral rest, and its red shadows stay rich (1.14).
pairs.fix: Make the coat a less orange chestnut. Let shadows on the belly and legs lean cool and violet from the sky, and keep them colorful, not muddy brown. Grey the fence and dirt so they are quieter than the horse.

pairs.difference: A: the shadow on the wood shifts to maroon-plum, and the book's page edge is cool lilac, which is a related shadow hue like the real cards. Its sticker colors are slightly too many (6.2 families). B: the hay and the ground are the same orange-yellow, and the bale's shadow is plain darker orange-brown. The card is only warm mass against a cyan strip, with no neutral rest on the bale.
pairs.fix: Make the hay a paler straw with grey-green dry stalks. Tint the ground shadow plum-violet with blue bounce from the wall, not darker orange.

pairs.difference: A: the copper lamp is a warm orange-brown against lime rays, with pale glass taking on background color. B: the steel pan is near neutral grey (subject chroma 0.023), with gold nuggets as the single accent. That low figure is correct local color for steel, and the lime bounce on the pan's rim matches the real cards. The two background treatments are nearly the same, so my vector gives no reason to choose.

A: the amber drink sits on a purple field with a cyan umbrella and a pink straw, so it is loud (background 0.24) but has clear complementary roles and pale glass as a rest. B: terracotta, hot pink and tan table are all warm (warm share 1.0, outside real), and the jug's chroma is above the real range. No cool note appears anywhere, and the jug's shadow is just deeper orange-red.
pairs.fix: Add a cool note by making the background a cooler berry or violet. Let the jug's shadow side pick up that violet, and keep the table a pale grey-beige.

pairs.difference: A: the orange and yellow towel on green has muted reddish shadows in the folds and two related hues, within range. B: the bandana is pure red over its whole area, with subject chroma 0.199 above the real range. Fold shadows are only a deeper pure red, and there are few hue families. Cyan shows through the white motifs in the lens as the only relief.
pairs.fix: Use a slightly faded, dusty red cloth. Let the fold shadows lean toward wine and plum, and keep the paisley off-white.

pairs.difference: A: pure orange sand and a pure orange wall with lime-green cactus, background 0.18 above real and only 2.2 hue families. Almost no neutral exists except small pink rocks, and the shadows go olive on the cactus and brown on the sand. B: the green slide on pink has blue rails, plus near-white tiles giving a large neutral rest, and 5.1 families.
pairs.fix: Make the sand a paler dusty beige and the sky wall a softer tone. Use a muted natural cactus green, and tint the sand shadow violet.

pairs.difference: A: red body, gold wheels, brown trim, tan seat and tan sand are all one warm group (warm share 0.71, above real). Shadows on the body and sand fall to duller brown-red (0.69), and only the sky is cool. B: pure primary red, yellow and blue on the coaster are loud (0.173), but the hue roles are clean and the shadows stay colored (0.90), with blue bounce on the rails.
pairs.fix: Paint the wheels in muted ochre and the body in a deeper, slightly dusty red. Let shadows under the coach go cool violet-blue from the sky, and make the desert paler and greyer.

pairs.difference: A: the barrel staves are one flat saturated orange with no brown wood color, unlike the natural brown real barrel. The card has only 2.7 hue families and shadow chroma 0.56 near the bottom, with the ground a dull mauve-pink. The purple bounce on the metal bands is its one believable note. B: red and white awning, gold posts, blue field and pale paving have clear roles and neutrals, with shadow chroma 0.94.
pairs.fix: Paint the barrel in natural medium-brown oak with varied plank tones, not pure orange. Deepen the shadows to a rich red-brown with violet from the wall.

pairs.difference: A: magenta-violet stripes are very loud (background 0.248, above real) against a tan hat with one teal accent, only 1.9 hue families, and the hat's shadow is plain brown. B: the coral sandals with yellow straps on teal have chroma balanced with the background, and 3.6 families, all within range. This is a weak call because B's shadows also stay in the coral hue.
pairs.fix: Calm the background to a softer, less saturated plum. Tint the hat's underside shadow with some of that violet instead of plain brown.

pairs.difference: A: the blue machine on violet is cool, with pink cans as accents and pale glass as a rest. Warm share is 0.03 but shadow chroma stays high at 1.28, and blue bounces onto the floor. B: the orange field, wood table and glowing flame pull the whole card warm (0.94). The lantern's slate body is the only neutral, and shadows on it are low in color (0.41, well below real), with no reflected color.
pairs.fix: Let the lantern's metal pick up blue-violet in the shadows and orange bounce on its edges. Cool the background toward a softer gold, and keep the table shadow reddish rather than grey.

pairs.difference: A: pure cobalt bag, pure lime grass and pure orange-yellow arcs are all at full chroma (background 0.179, at the top of range), so hero and background are equally loud with no neutral. The bag's shadow is a single dark navy mass. B: pale pink cabinet and teal room, with cream-grey neutrals and lavender shadows in the lens to rest the eye, though many toy colors push the family count.
pairs.fix: Make the bag a slightly dusty blue and the grass a softer natural green. Lower the sky to a gentle pale yellow, and add a quiet neutral such as grey-beige canvas on the bag's trim.

pattern: Three things still give generated cards away. Everything is pushed to the object's purest hue: orange wood, pure red cloth, lime grass. Shadows stay in the same hue, only darker, or go dull brown, where real cards shift them toward a related violet, plum or blue picked up from the background. Whites and neutrals turn cream or warm, or vanish, so hero and background are equally loud and the card has little neutral area to rest the eye.
